competitors.name: Yough
competitors.action: Founders Row invested in Yough as the brand launched its Greek-yogurt-dough frozen pizzas nationwide at Target, putting the better-for-you concept into just under 2,000 stores out of the gate.

competitors.name: California Pizza Kitchen
competitors.action: California Pizza Kitchen said it is expanding its retail business beyond frozen pizza for the first time since 1999, while also widening Nestle-led frozen pizza distribution across Latin America and pushing further into Asia.

competitors.name: Amy's Kitchen
competitors.action: Amy's Kitchen promoted longtime operator Paul Schiefer to CEO, signaling a new growth chapter for one of frozen retail's most credible premium brands as it emphasizes innovation, sustainability, and operational discipline across a business nearing $1 billion in retail sales.

trends.topic: Frozen pizza and adjacent frozen CPG are rewarding sharper platforms, not generic premium claims
trends.magnitude: Yough is scaling a high-protein reformulation into ~2,000 Target doors, CPK is extending restaurant brand equity beyond pizza while expanding internationally, and Amy's is tightening leadership around innovation plus operating performance.
trends.context: For Real Dough, the signal is that freezer winners are pairing product quality with a very legible growth story, either functional nutrition, brand-platform extension, or disciplined premium trust.

market_data.value: 57,000+ stores and approaching $1 billion in retail sales

breaking.headline: Today's cleanest signal is that frozen pizza growth is clustering around clearer strategic stories
breaking.impact: High-protein reformulation, restaurant-brand line extension, and premium frozen leadership upgrades are all getting real capital and shelf support. Real Dough should keep building around a specific retail promise buyers can repeat in one sentence, not a broad artisan claim.
